	<article id="post-34568" class="post-34568 post type-post status-publish format-standard has-post-thumbnail hentry category-bitly-products" role="article" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/BlogPosting">
		
			
		<header class="article-header">

						<h1 class="h0 entry-title single-title" itemprop="headline">Introducing Bitly Assist and Weekly Insights: Clearer Insights, Faster Decisions</h1>
						<div class="post-meta">
							
<p class="p0">
	 <span class="post-date">April 2, 2026</span>
</p>							<p class="p0"> 
								<svg width="8" height="8" viewBox="0 0 8 8" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
									<circle cx="4" cy="4" r="4" fill="#6C6965"/>
								</svg>
								<span id="time"></span> min read							</p>
						</div>
											</div>
					<div class="cell large-6">
						<div class="post-hero"><img width="1200" height="675" src="https://d3gribjq2zt3oj.cloudfront.net/blog-hub/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/featured-image.png" class="attachment-full size-full wp-post-image" alt="" decoding="async" fetchpriority="high" /></div>
					</div>
				</div>
			</div>
		</header> <!-- end article header -->
				<section class="entry-content" itemprop="text">
			<div class="grid-container post-content-inner">
				<div class="inner-content grid-x grid-margin-x grid-padding-x  align-center">
					<div id="blog-content" class="cell large-8 small-order-2 large-order-1">

						
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">If you’ve ever opened your analytics dashboard and thought to yourself, “<em>I know the numbers are here, but I don’t know what to do with them,”</em> you’re not alone. Marketing teams today are surrounded by performance data, yet still spend too much time searching for answers, piecing together reports, and trying to figure out what actions will actually move the needle.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">That challenge tends to show up in the same ways: insights are hard to surface, analysis requires manual effort, and even when you have the numbers, it’s not always clear what to do next.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">That’s why we’re excited to introduce <strong>Bitly Assist </strong>and <strong>Weekly Insights</strong>—a new way to create, analyze, and optimize your links and QR Codes with less effort and more clarity. Together, these new features help you move from raw data to real direction, all within the workflows you already use.</p>





<h2 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-what-is-bitly-assist"><strong>What is Bitly Assist?</strong></h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><a href="https://bitly.com/pages/ai/bitly-assist">Bitly Assist</a> is an AI-powered chat assistant built directly into Bitly that lets you ask questions about your link and QR Code performance—and get clear answers in seconds. It also helps you create <a href="https://bitly.com/pages/products/url-shortener">links</a> and <a href="https://bitly.com/pages/products/qr-codes">QR Codes</a> conversationally, so you can move from idea to execution without friction.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Instead of clicking through filters or exporting data, you can ask questions in plain language and get relevant, data-backed answers instantly. Whether you’re building out a report, comparing campaigns, or digging into specific links, Bitly Assist helps you move from question to understanding in seconds.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">This matters because most analytics workflows break down before insight ever happens. Data gets buried and the effort required to find answers slows teams down. Bitly Assist removes that friction, making it easier to explore your data the way you naturally think—through questions and follow-ups.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img decoding="async" width="1999" height="1199" src="https://d3gribjq2zt3oj.cloudfront.net/blog-hub/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-within-the-blog-post.png" alt="" class="wp-image-34574"/></figure>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Your fastest path to uncovering what works</strong></h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Bitly Assist gives you a faster, more intuitive way to work with your link and QR Code data. Instead of building reports manually, you can simply ask questions and get answers in seconds. When stakeholders need answers on the fly, you can quickly pull the data you need without rebuilding reports from scratch.<br><br>Ezra Varley, a communications specialist at Pasado’s Safe Haven, <a href="https://bitly.com/pages/resources/case-studies/pasado-safe-haven/">uses Bitly Assist to streamline reporting</a> and get answers from his data faster. As he shared, “It happens in a minute… It was really intuitive—pretty direct, which was really nice.”</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Because it’s embedded in your existing workflow, Bitly Assist is always available right when questions come up. Whether you’re reviewing performance, building a campaign, or responding to a stakeholder request, you can get the answers you need without slowing down. For Ezra, that speed is critical in a fast-moving environment. “If I need to get information to people in the same-day… I would definitely use Bitly Assist,” he said.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Where to find Bitly Assist: </strong></p>



<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li>Login to your Bitly account<br><br></li>



<li>Look at the top menu bar next to your name <br><br></li>



<li>Click on the icon with three stars<br><br></li>



<li>Ask a question about your link or QR Code performance to begin exploring</li>
</ul>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading" id="what-are-weekly-insights?"><strong>What are Weekly Insights? </strong></h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Weekly Insights is a new experience within <a href="https://bitly.com/pages/products/analytics">Bitly Analytics</a> that automatically highlights meaningful changes in your performance from the prior week, so you can quickly understand what’s working and what’s not.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Refreshed on a weekly basis, these insights bring the most important signals to the surface. It identifies patterns across your links, referrers, geographies, devices, and more, helping you focus on the trends that actually matter.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">This is where many teams struggle today. Performance data is available, but it’s fragmented and easy to overlook. Weekly Insights closes that gap by making insights more visible, more contextual, and easier to act on. </p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Your next best campaign starts here</strong></h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Knowing what happened is helpful. Knowing what to do next is what actually moves your performance forward. But for many marketers, it’s still difficult to answer the most important question: is this actually resonating with my audience?</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Weekly Insights is designed to surface the signals that matter most and turn them into direction you can act on. Instead of trying to interpret trends on your own, you get a clear view of what’s changing, what’s working, and where there’s an opportunity to improve.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Over time, this makes it easier to spot patterns, refine your strategy, and build stronger campaigns with every iteration.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Where to find Weekly Insights: </strong></p>



<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li>Login to your Bitly account<br><br></li>



<li>Navigate to the Analytics page<br><br></li>



<li>Look for the Insights panel <br><br></li>



<li>Review weekly highlights, performance changes, and ask Bitly Assist for further analysis</li>
</ul>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading" id="making-every-insight-count"><strong>Making every insight count</strong></h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The real value of Bitly Assist and Weekly Insights comes from how they work together. Bitly Assist helps you answer specific questions in the moment. Weekly Insights ensures you don’t miss important changes between those moments. Together, they create a more complete and continuous understanding of your performance where you can: </p>



<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li>Get answers from your data in seconds, without manual work<br><br></li>



<li>Surface meaningful performance changes automatically<br><br></li>



<li>Understand what’s driving engagement across campaigns and channels<br><br></li>



<li>Act on insights immediately within the same workflow </li>
</ul>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">If a link is gaining traction, you can quickly build on that momentum. If engagement shifts across a channel or region, you can investigate and adjust. And when new questions come up, you can answer them instantly without restarting your workflow. Over time, this creates a feedback loop where your data doesn’t just inform reporting—it actively improves your campaigns.</p>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading" id="start-exploring-your-data-today"><strong>Start exploring your data today</strong></h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Bitly Assist and Weekly Insights are now available to all Bitly customers on paid plans. If you’re ready to spend less time searching for insights and more time acting on them, <a href="https://bitly.com/a/sign_in">log in to Bitly today </a>and start exploring Bitly Assist and Weekly Insights.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">These launches are an important step toward making Bitly more intuitive, more intelligent, and more deeply embedded in how you already work. As AI continues to reshape how teams analyze performance and optimize campaigns, we’ll keep expanding these experiences with more powerful workflows, deeper insights, and smarter recommendations.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">We’re excited about what this unlocks for teams today—and even more excited about what’s ahead!</p>

Clearer Insights, Faster Decisions April 2, 2026 min read If you’ve ever opened your analytics dashboard and thought to yourself, “ I know the numbers are here, but I don’t know what to do with them,” you’re not alone. Marketing teams today are surrounded by performance data, yet still spend too much time searching for answers, piecing together reports, and trying to figure out what actions will actually move the needle. That challenge tends to show up in the same ways: insights are hard to surface, analysis requires manual effort, and even when you have the numbers, it’s not always clear what to do next. That’s why we’re excited to introduce Bitly Assist and Weekly Insights —a new way to create, analyze, and optimize your links and QR Codes with less effort and more clarity. Together, these new features help you move from raw data to real direction, all within the workflows you already use. What is Bitly Assist? Bitly Assist is an AI-powered chat assistant built directly into Bitly that lets you ask questions about your link and QR Code performance—and get clear answers in seconds. It also helps you create links and QR Codes conversationally, so you can move from idea to execution without friction. Instead of clicking through filters or exporting data, you can ask questions in plain language and get relevant, data-backed answers instantly. Whether you’re building out a report, comparing campaigns, or digging into specific links, Bitly Assist helps you move from question to understanding in seconds. This matters because most analytics workflows break down before insight ever happens. Data gets buried and the effort required to find answers slows teams down. Bitly Assist removes that friction, making it easier to explore your data the way you naturally think—through questions and follow-ups. Your fastest path to uncovering what works Bitly Assist gives you a faster, more intuitive way to work with your link and QR Code data. Instead of building reports manually, you can simply ask questions and get answers in seconds. When stakeholders need answers on the fly, you can quickly pull the data you need without rebuilding reports from scratch. Ezra Varley, a communications specialist at Pasado’s Safe Haven, uses Bitly Assist to streamline reporting and get answers from his data faster. As he shared, “It happens in a minute… It was really intuitive—pretty direct, which was really nice.” Because it’s embedded in your existing workflow, Bitly Assist is always available right when questions come up. Whether you’re reviewing performance, building a campaign, or responding to a stakeholder request, you can get the answers you need without slowing down. For Ezra, that speed is critical in a fast-moving environment. “If I need to get information to people in the same-day… I would definitely use Bitly Assist,” he said. Where to find Bitly Assist:  Login to your Bitly account Look at the top menu bar next to your name  Click on the icon with three stars Ask a question about your link or QR Code performance to begin exploring What are Weekly Insights?  Weekly Insights is a new experience within Bitly Analytics that automatically highlights meaningful changes in your performance from the prior week, so you can quickly understand what’s working and what’s not. Refreshed on a weekly basis, these insights bring the most important signals to the surface. It identifies patterns across your links, referrers, geographies, devices, and more, helping you focus on the trends that actually matter. This is where many teams struggle today. Performance data is available, but it’s fragmented and easy to overlook. Weekly Insights closes that gap by making insights more visible, more contextual, and easier to act on.  Your next best campaign starts here Knowing what happened is helpful. Knowing what to do next is what actually moves your performance forward. But for many marketers, it’s still difficult to answer the most important question: is this actually resonating with my audience? Weekly Insights is designed to surface the signals that matter most and turn them into direction you can act on. Instead of trying to interpret trends on your own, you get a clear view of what’s changing, what’s working, and where there’s an opportunity to improve. Over time, this makes it easier to spot patterns, refine your strategy, and build stronger campaigns with every iteration. Where to find Weekly Insights:  Login to your Bitly account Navigate to the Analytics page Look for the Insights panel  Review weekly highlights, performance changes, and ask Bitly Assist for further analysis Making every insight count The real value of Bitly Assist and Weekly Insights comes from how they work together. Bitly Assist helps you answer specific questions in the moment. Weekly Insights ensures you don’t miss important changes between those moments. Together, they create a more complete and continuous understanding of your performance where you can:  Get answers from your data in seconds, without manual work Surface meaningful performance changes automatically Understand what’s driving engagement across campaigns and channels Act on insights immediately within the same workflow  If a link is gaining traction, you can quickly build on that momentum. If engagement shifts across a channel or region, you can investigate and adjust. And when new questions come up, you can answer them instantly without restarting your workflow. Over time, this creates a feedback loop where your data doesn’t just inform reporting—it actively improves your campaigns. Start exploring your data today Bitly Assist and Weekly Insights are now available to all Bitly customers on paid plans. If you’re ready to spend less time searching for insights and more time acting on them, log in to Bitly today and start exploring Bitly Assist and Weekly Insights. These launches are an important step toward making Bitly more intuitive, more intelligent, and more deeply embedded in how you already work. As AI continues to reshape how teams analyze performance and optimize campaigns, we’ll keep expanding these experiences with more powerful workflows, deeper insights, and smarter recommendations. We’re excited about what this unlocks for teams today—and even more excited about what’s ahead! Table of contents: What is Bitly Assist? 					<div class="block-intro">
				<h3 class="h3" style="text-align: center">Frequently asked questions (FAQs)</h3>

				<div class="inner-content grid-x grid-margin-x">

								<div class="accordion" data-accordion data-allow-all-closed="true">
										<div class="accordion-item" data-accordion-item itemprop="mainEntity" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Question">
						<a class="accordion-title" tabindex="0">
							<div itemprop="name">What is a QR Code?</div>
						</a>
						<div class="accordion-content" tabindex="0" data-tab-content itemprop="acceptedAnswer" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Answer">
							<div itemprop="text">
								<p>A QR Code (Quick Response Code) is a type of barcode that people can scan using their smartphone cameras to quickly access information via URL—product information, contact details, menus, and other helpful resources for customers! Due to their convenience and versatility, QR Codes are widely used to personalize marketing campaigns, improve product packaging, promote events, and share shipping or tracking information.</p>
							</div>
						</div>
					</div>
										<div class="accordion-item" data-accordion-item itemprop="mainEntity" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Question">
						<a class="accordion-title" tabindex="0">
							<div itemprop="name">How can I create a QR Code with Bitly?</div>
						</a>
						<div class="accordion-content" tabindex="0" data-tab-content itemprop="acceptedAnswer" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Answer">
							<div itemprop="text">
								<p>Creating a QR Code with Bitly is quick and simple.</p>
<ol>
<li>Sign up for or sign into your Bitly account.</li>
<li>Go to <strong>Create new</strong> and select <strong>QR Code</strong> from the options.</li>
<li>Enter the <strong>Destination URL</strong> for the information you’d like to encode (and any code details if applicable, like customized domain or back-half options for the short link generated alongside your QR Code).</li>
<li>Select <strong>Design your code</strong> and customize your QR Code style, colors, logo (or center text), frame, corners, and branding (available in some plans).</li>
<li>Select <strong>Create your code</strong> and that’s it—you’re ready to go! You can download your code in JPEG, PNG, or SVG format or copy it directly from the Bitly platform.</li>
</ol>
<p>Depending on your Bitly plan, you can create up to 200 Bitly QR Codes each month. And for brands needing hundreds or thousands of codes per month (or more), our custom enterprise solutions are ideal!</p>
							</div>
						</div>
					</div>
										<div class="accordion-item" data-accordion-item itemprop="mainEntity" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Question">
						<a class="accordion-title" tabindex="0">
							<div itemprop="name">What types of content can I link to with a Bitly QR Code?</div>
						</a>
						<div class="accordion-content" tabindex="0" data-tab-content itemprop="acceptedAnswer" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Answer">
							<div itemprop="text">
								<p>Bitly QR Codes can link to anything with a URL attached. This means you can create customized QR Codes that link to specific web pages, digital experiences, PDFs hosted on websites, and promotional content.</p>
<p>Brands can use Bitly QR Codes nearly everywhere that information is shared:</p>
<ul>
<li>Product packaging</li>
<li>Order confirmations</li>
<li>SMS marketing campaigns</li>
<li>Digital posters</li>
<li>Social media</li>
<li>Billboards</li>
<li>Industry-specific media, like restaurant menus or real estate listings</li>
</ul>
							</div>
						</div>
					</div>
										<div class="accordion-item" data-accordion-item itemprop="mainEntity" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Question">
						<a class="accordion-title" tabindex="0">
							<div itemprop="name">Can I customize the design of my QR Code?</div>
						</a>
						<div class="accordion-content" tabindex="0" data-tab-content itemprop="acceptedAnswer" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Answer">
							<div itemprop="text">
								<p>Yes! It’s easy to customize the look of your QR Code with Bitly’s QR Code generator. In the ‘Design your code’ step of the process outlined above, you can customize:</p>
<ul>
<li>Colors and gradients</li>
<li>Dot patterns</li>
<li>Frames</li>
<li>Corners</li>
<li>Brand logos (or custom images)</li>
<li>Accompanying text</li>
</ul>
<p>You can also save your current design to quickly create the same look again!</p>
<p>*Note that some of these features are only included in Bitly paid plans. With upgraded plans, you have more color, gradient, pattern, and frame options for every QR Code you create.</p>
							</div>
						</div>
					</div>
										<div class="accordion-item" data-accordion-item itemprop="mainEntity" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Question">
						<a class="accordion-title" tabindex="0">
							<div itemprop="name">Do Bitly QR Codes ever expire?</div>
						</a>
						<div class="accordion-content" tabindex="0" data-tab-content itemprop="acceptedAnswer" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Answer">
							<div itemprop="text">
								<p>Bitly QR Codes don’t expire on their own. If you want one to stop working on a schedule, set an expiration date and time during or after creation, available on paid plans. You can also redirect a QR Code to a new URL at any time or delete the link behind it to turn it off.</p>
							</div>
						</div>
					</div>
										<div class="accordion-item" data-accordion-item itemprop="mainEntity" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Question">
						<a class="accordion-title" tabindex="0">
							<div itemprop="name">How many times can a QR Code be scanned?</div>
						</a>
						<div class="accordion-content" tabindex="0" data-tab-content itemprop="acceptedAnswer" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Answer">
							<div itemprop="text">
								<p>As many times as you’d like! No matter which Bitly plan you sign up for, all Bitly QR Codes can be scanned an unlimited number of times. This accessibility makes them suitable for both large-scale and small-scale campaigns.</p>
							</div>
						</div>
					</div>
										<div class="accordion-item" data-accordion-item itemprop="mainEntity" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Question">
						<a class="accordion-title" tabindex="0">
							<div itemprop="name">How can I track the performance of my Bitly QR Codes?</div>
						</a>
						<div class="accordion-content" tabindex="0" data-tab-content itemprop="acceptedAnswer" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Answer">
							<div itemprop="text">
								<p>Bitly’s built-in dashboard gives you everything you need. View scan data for individual codes or see your top performers in the QR Code section of your paid Bitly account.</p>
<p>For every QR Code on a <a href="https://bitly.com/pages/pricing">paid Bitly plan</a>, you can track information like:</p>
<ul>
<li>Total scans</li>
<li>Scan history</li>
<li>Scans by day</li>
<li>Scans by location</li>
<li>Scans by browser</li>
<li>Scans by operating system (OS)</li>
</ul>
<p>Ask Bitly Assist about your scan performance in plain language, and let Weekly Insights surface what changed and what to do next.</p>
							</div>
						</div>
					</div>

We’re a small NPO. There are 5 of us, doing the work of 10 people. So anything to make our lives easier – is important. For example – Pages. We have a Page for our Instagram. It is so nice to be able to ‘turn off one of our programs’ and when we need it – turn it back on. Ronni Eloff Chief Information and Tech Officer, This is Jane Project UE verified: 03/31/2025 Survey conducted by UserEvidence. https://uevi.co/3047WRGF Frequently asked questions (FAQs) What is a QR Code? A QR Code (Quick Response Code) is a type of barcode that people can scan using their smartphone cameras to quickly access information via URL—product information, contact details, menus, and other helpful resources for customers! Due to their convenience and versatility, QR Codes are widely used to personalize marketing campaigns, improve product packaging, promote events, and share shipping or tracking information. How can I create a QR Code with Bitly? Creating a QR Code with Bitly is quick and simple. Sign up for or sign into your Bitly account. Go to Create new and select QR Code from the options. Enter the Destination URL for the information you’d like to encode (and any code details if applicable, like customized domain or back-half options for the short link generated alongside your QR Code). Select Design your code and customize your QR Code style, colors, logo (or center text), frame, corners, and branding (available in some plans). Select Create your code and that’s it—you’re ready to go! You can download your code in JPEG, PNG, or SVG format or copy it directly from the Bitly platform. Depending on your Bitly plan, you can create up to 200 Bitly QR Codes each month. And for brands needing hundreds or thousands of codes per month (or more), our custom enterprise solutions are ideal! What types of content can I link to with a Bitly QR Code? Bitly QR Codes can link to anything with a URL attached. This means you can create customized QR Codes that link to specific web pages, digital experiences, PDFs hosted on websites, and promotional content. Brands can use Bitly QR Codes nearly everywhere that information is shared: Product packaging Order confirmations SMS marketing campaigns Digital posters Social media Billboards Industry-specific media, like restaurant menus or real estate listings Can I customize the design of my QR Code? Yes! It’s easy to customize the look of your QR Code with Bitly’s QR Code generator. In the ‘Design your code’ step of the process outlined above, you can customize: Colors and gradients Dot patterns Frames Corners Brand logos (or custom images) Accompanying text You can also save your current design to quickly create the same look again! *Note that some of these features are only included in Bitly paid plans. With upgraded plans, you have more color, gradient, pattern, and frame options for every QR Code you create. Do Bitly QR Codes ever expire? Bitly QR Codes don’t expire on their own. If you want one to stop working on a schedule, set an expiration date and time during or after creation, available on paid plans. You can also redirect a QR Code to a new URL at any time or delete the link behind it to turn it off. How many times can a QR Code be scanned? As many times as you’d like! No matter which Bitly plan you sign up for, all Bitly QR Codes can be scanned an unlimited number of times. This accessibility makes them suitable for both large-scale and small-scale campaigns. How can I track the performance of my Bitly QR Codes? Bitly’s built-in dashboard gives you everything you need. View scan data for individual codes or see your top performers in the QR Code section of your paid Bitly account. For every QR Code on a paid Bitly plan , you can track information like: Total scans Scan history Scans by day Scans by location Scans by browser Scans by operating system (OS) Ask Bitly Assist about your scan performance in plain language, and let Weekly Insights surface what changed and what to do next. <script>
jQuery(document).ready(function ($) {
    // setup token if not present
    var _xsrf = document.cookie.match("\\b_xsrf=([^;]*)\\b"),
      _xsrf = _xsrf ? _xsrf[1] : undefined;

    endPointURL = "https:\/\/" + location.hostname + '/data/geo';
 
    // check if user is in experiment
    var options = {
      url: endPointURL,
      timeout: 12000,
      dataType: "json",
      traditional: true,
      beforeSend: function (XMLHttpRequest) {
        XMLHttpRequest.setRequestHeader("X-XSRFToken", _xsrf);
      },
      success: function (res) {
        try {
          variation = res.country_code;
        } catch (error) {
          variation = "US";
        }
		  
        if (variation == "ID" || variation == "IN" || variation == "BD" ) {
			
			$('body').addClass('entitlement-case');
			if($('#comparison-table').length > 0) {
				$('.plan-column:first-child() .specs ul li:nth-child(2) strong').text('50');
				newtxt = $('#comparison-table tbody:nth-child(3) tr:nth-child(2) td:nth-child(2)').text().replace('5','50');
				$('#comparison-table tbody:nth-child(3) tr:nth-child(2) td:nth-child(2)').text(newtxt);
			}
			
        }

		if (variation == "BR"){
			$('.plan-column.free .plan-price.month .currency').text('$0');
				$('.plan-column.free .plan-price.year .currency').text('$0');
				$('.plan-column.core .plan-price.month .currency').text('$5');
				$('.plan-column.core .plan-price.month small .currency').text('$60');
				// grownth
				$('.plan-column.growth .plan-price.month .currency').text('$15');
				$('.plan-column.growth .plan-price.month small .currency').text('$180');
				$('.plan-column.growth .plan-price.year .currency').text('$17');
				// Premium
				$('.plan-column.premium .plan-price.month .currency').text('$100');
				$('.plan-column.premium .plan-price.month small .currency').text('$1200');
				$('.plan-column.premium .plan-price.year .currency').text('$150');	
				///pricint bottom
				// core
				$('#free-plan-annual-price, #free-plan-monthly-price').html('$0<sub>/mo<strong>');	
				$('#core-plan-annual-price').html('$5<sub>/mo<strong>($60 annually)');
				// grownth
				$('#growth-plan-annual-price').html('$15<sub>/mo<strong>($180 annually)');
				$('#growth-plan-monthly-price').html('$17.5<sub>/mo');
				// Premium
				$('#premium-plan-annual-price').html('$100<sub>/mo<strong>($1,200 annually)');
				$('#premium-plan-monthly-price').html('$150<sub>/mo');
			
		}
        
      },
      error: function (res) {
        console.log('geo-call');
      },
    };
    $.ajax(options);
});

Geography, referrer, and device tracking Cross-channel analytics dashboards AI-powered analytics and insights Campaign performance and UTMs Get started for free Learn more Life at Bitly For over a decade, we’ve been the point of connection for sharers of digital information and their audiences. We pride ourselves in being a platform that is a catalyst for connections and we carry that commitment across everything we do. Our core values Bitizens believe in action, progress and growth. Our values embody this. Be a catalyst As an innovative technology company, we build our products to be catalysts for connection and encourage our team to be catalysts for change and innovation. Take ownership In our highly collaborative culture, individual accountability is critical. While depending on each other to solve our customers’ most challenging problems, we celebrate the wins and failures together. Champion inclusion Our products bring people together across backgrounds and abilities. We’re built on the belief that inclusion drives progress—and that our differences make us stronger. Everyone deserves the opportunity to belong, contribute, and thrive. Have fun Building a memorable work experience comes both through driving meaningful impact while also not taking ourselves too seriously. We work hard but that doesn’t mean we don’t have fun. Show integrity We don’t cut corners. We don’t look for the easy way out. We approach every day with a shared mindset – let’s do the right thing, even if it’s the harder thing. Inclusion at Bitly Creating human connection starts with a culture of inclusion, accessibility, and continuous learning. These values are part of who we are—and we’re committed to making Bitly an even better place to work by growing in each of these areas. Learn more Meet the Leadership Team Jerome Alabado VP, Financial Planning & Analysis LinkedIn Jerome is Bitly’s VP of Financial Planning and Analysis. He is focused on financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, and key business metric analysis that support Bitly’s growth and profitability objectives. Before Bitly, Jerome held leadership roles at public companies and high-growth startups, most recently as VP of Finance at ActiveCampaign. Manu Jain VP, Data LinkedIn Manu is Bitly’s VP of Data. He is responsible for building Bitly’s comprehensive data platform that empowers the company with insights, fuels innovation, enhances user experience, and helps chart new pathways. Before Bitly, Manu held leadership roles in the data and analytics space at PayPal, Wayfair, Meta and McKinsey. Shannon Jankun VP, Human Resources LinkedIn Shannon is Bitly’s VP of Human Resources. She is focused on talent management, employee relations, and organizational development initiatives in support of an engaged, inclusive and high-performing culture. Before Bitly, Shannon held progressive HR roles, most recently at Ahold Delhaize, with a focus on strategic business partnering. Peter Krivkovich Chief Executive Officer LinkedIn Peter is Bitly’s CEO, where he leads the company’s strategic vision, innovation roadmap, and growth initiatives. Prior to this role, Peter served as the company’s Chief Financial Officer, where he played a critical role in scaling the business, optimizing operations, and building a strong foundation for sustainable growth. Prior to joining Bitly, Peter was the Co-Founder, CFO and former CEO of NextRoll. Oran Mizrahi VP, Finance LinkedIn Oran is Bitly’s VP of Finance. She oversees all aspects of finance and is responsible for scaling the company’s global finance organization to foster Bitly’s growth. Before Bitly, Oran held roles at LivePerson and Ernst and Young. Sam Oh VP, Acquisition LinkedIn Sam is Bitly’s VP of Acquisition. He focuses on driving revenue by connecting the value of our platform and products to our current and new customers. Before Bitly, Sam served marketing teams at Seismic, Lessonly, and Craftsy. Luke Reynebeau VP, Customer & Retention Marketing LinkedIn Luke is Bitly’s VP of Customer and Retention Marketing. His focus is on user engagement programs, partner and ecosystem marketing and customer marketing initiatives aligned to both customer experience and revenue goals. Prior to joining Bitly, Luke worked in marketing leadership roles in SaaS scale-ups and startups, including overseeing partner and customer marketing at Sprout Social during its growth from startup to IPO. Michael Richman VP, Engineering LinkedIn Michael is Bitly’s VP of Engineering focused on Platform & Infrastructure. He oversees teams responsible for stability, scalability, distributed systems, modernization, and Trust & Safety. Michael joined Bitly in 2010 to build out the first paid offering and has led both Platform and Application Development teams. Prior to Bitly, Michael rose through the engineering ranks at AOL where he worked on a variety of properties including AIM, MapQuest, and AOL.com. Tara Robertson Chief Commercial Officer LinkedIn Tara Robertson is Bitly’s Chief Commercial Officer. She manages all marketing, sales, and customer success matters for the company–creating and communicating value to millions of customers. Before Bitly, Tara held roles at Teamwork, Sprout Social Inc. and Hotjar. Kelsey Stevenson Chief Product Officer LinkedIn Kelsey is Bitly’s Chief Product Officer. She’s focused on setting the product vision, creating a product strategy aligned with Bitly’s company goals and delivering product solutions that solve customer pain points. Prior to joining Bitly, Kelsey led product teams at Cloud Elements and spent time as a product management consultant at Slalom. Raphael Syed VP, Engineering LinkedIn Rapha is Bitly’s VP of Engineering. He is focused on building reliable, scalable, and secure systems for Bitly customers and users. He works to enhance technical and process efficiency, and is involved in leading the security and compliance endeavors from an engineering viewpoint. Before joining Bitly, he was responsible for managing the engineering org at Chronext, a prominent marketplace for luxury watch trading. Matt Young Chief Technology Officer LinkedIn Matt is Bitly’s Chief Technology Officer, where he leads the Engineering and Data organizations, ensuring consistent high-quality delivery and sustainable long-term growth across the company’s platforms and services. Before Bitly, Matt served as Chief Executive Officer at UserVoice, where he guided product direction, team execution, and strategic growth for the customer feedback and engagement platform.
